open_questions: Why depth in sector 33 (TESS-SPOC) is 675 ppm while sector 6 (SPOC 2-min) is 1437 ppm and sector 87 (QLP) is 1700 ppm - is it spot crossing, dilution/crowding change, or dilution from a blended EB?
Confirm on-target localisation with high-SNR difference imaging (centroid_all) vs a residual blended signal, given inconclusive centroid
Rule out spot modulation linked to RUWE=1.502 vs transit depth change with follow-up photometry at known period 13.4 d
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 3.5-hour, flat-ish dip every 13.4 days consistent with a ~2.7 Earth-radius planet on a K-dwarf, with no odd-even or secondary eclipse. The depth, however, is not steady: it is about half as deep in one sector as the other two, and the sky position of the dip remains inconclusive. That makes a planet possible but not proven; additional on-target monitoring is needed to see if the depth stabilises and confirm the signal is not blended or spot-driven.
